name: Xoşkîn
description: Xoşkîn is a Kurdish trick-taking card game similar to 3-player double-deck Pinochle. Played in eastern/southeastern Turkey (Northern Kurdistan). Features bidding and melds. Also known as Nezere or Pinîkêr. Name possibly derived from English 'Auction' via 'Okşin'.

overview.description: Xoşkîn is a Kurdish trick-taking card game similar to 3-player double-deck Pinochle. Played in eastern/southeastern Turkey (Northern Kurdistan). Features bidding and melds. Also known as Nezere or Pinîkêr. Name possibly derived from English 'Auction' via 'Okşin'.

history.origins: This Kurdish trick-taking game with bidding is played in the eastern and south-eastern parts of Turkey, unofficially known as northern Kurdistan. Xoşkîn is almost identical to the American game of three-handed double deck Pinochle; the alternative name Pinîkêr reflects that. As Levent Suberk suggested, the name Xoşkîn likely derives from the English 'Auction', probably via 'Okşin'. A version played by Turkish workers in Düsseldorf has been documented by Thomas Beil.
timeline: 20th century: Kurdish adaptation of American three-handed double-deck Pinochle in eastern Turkey.
history.cultural: Played in Kurdish communities of Eastern Turkey.

setup.dealing: Cards dealt to 3 players with widow.

rules.objective: Win the most card points through bidding, meld declarations, and trick play; the highest total score wins the game.
rules.gameplay: Bidding for contract. Winner takes widow, discards. Declare melds for points. Play tricks. Must follow suit and trump. Card point values for A, 10, K, Q, J.

scoring.description: Melds + card points from tricks. Penalties for failed contracts.
scoring.winCondition: Win card points through tricks and declare melds.
